Article Title: 21 Bangladesh nationals detained in J&K’s Ramban
Article Text:

JAMMU: At least 21 Bangladesh nationals, including four women and seven minors, were detained in J&K’s Ramban district last week. Officials were questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement to the Union Territory, official sources said Monday.The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive in Banihal on Aug 1, as no vehicle apart from those in Amarnath convoys is currently being allowed to move towards Kashmir in view of rain-triggered landslides and mudslides.Those detained are aged between two years and 38 years. “Upon verification, none of them could produce any valid identity or travel document establishing their lawful entry into or presence within Indian territory,” said an official source.“During preliminary questioning, the detained individuals disclosed that they had crossed the international border and entered India through Assam, from where they travelled to Jammu via train. They were moving towards Kashmir in search of employment,” the source added.Investigators were probing whether any local or interstate network was involved in assisting the movement of these illegal immigrants.
Article Summary: At least 21 Bangladesh nationals, including four women and seven minors, were detained in J&K’s Ramban district last week. Officials were questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement to the Union Territory. Those detained are aged between two years and 38 years.

Article Title: SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Inter-state row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to attorney general R Venkataramani's proposal for amicable implementation of a 15-year-old Supreme Court decree settling Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh made SC observe, "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard. "Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that he had extensive consultations with Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Union ministry of power after getting the records examined by CAG for independent determination of the historical capital cost liability."...a mutually workable settlement framework has been evolved. It envisages a cashless settlement, wherein the respective claims and liabilities are proposed to be adjusted through in-kind settlement of energy arrears and set-off of capital cost liability, thereby obviating the need for any direct financial transaction between the states," the AG said.Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Balbir Singh, appearing for Himachal and Haryana, respectively, said they were agreeable with the AG's settlement proposal for implementation of the decree, which was passed by the SC in 2011 on an original suit filed by Himachal 30 years ago seeking settlement of assets on division of Punjab in 1966.For Punjab, senior advocate Nidhesh Gupta said the state had key concerns over workability of the AG's proposal and said the state would stand to lose substantially.Given the fact that it is a 15-year-old decree passed on a 30-year-old original suit seeking resolution of a 60-year-old inter-state dispute, the bench said, "Your state has a habit of defying decrees...""There is a decree in Himachal's favour. When we order implement, it will be with interest from 2011. We will not allow them to be deprived of the fruits of the decree. If you settle, it is well and good. Otherwise, be ready for consequences." It posted the matter for hearing on Aug 12.In its July 30 order, the bench said, "While the states of Himachal and Haryana have graciously agreed in principle to the proposal, the state of Punjab has raised objections thereto. In the interest of justice, two weeks time is granted to Punjab to reconsider and clarify its stand."The AG's proposal had said, "Punjab and Haryana will provide 13,066 MU of energy arrears to HP at 871 MU per annum over 15 lean seasons (Oct-March), in the inter-se ratio of 58:42 (Bhakra Nangal project) and 60:40 (Beas projects). HP to pay BBMB-determined charges for the year in which each tranche is received."HP's liability (7.19% of composite Punjab) towards the capital cost of Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects - being the unreimbursed share of loan servicing by Punjab and Haryana since 1966-67 - be assessed at Rs 420.7 crore (Punjab: Rs 249.2 crore; Haryana: Rs 171.5 crore). The capital cost liability could be considered to set off against part of HP's energy arrear receivables.At the rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, the units to be offset is approximately 1093 MUs. "SC on Sept 27, 2011 (Justices R V Raveendran and A K Patnaik) had decreed the suit in favour of HP by ruling, "The state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite state of Punjab from the Bhakra Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II."
Article Summary: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to amicable implementation of 15-year-old Supreme Court decree. Decree settled Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh. "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard," says SC.

Article Title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
Article Text:
The Census is also likely to collect passport numbers (where available) and Aadhaar numbers voluntarily.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 — which will capture caste for the first time since 1931, and most likely also record the date and birthplace of parents, along with the respondent’s passport number (where available) and Aadhaar number (voluntary) — will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17.A home ministry notification on Monday said the population enumeration exercise in snow-bound areas of the four northern states/UTs will run from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of August 17-30. This means that the questionnaire for Phase 2 of Census will also be notified soon.According to sources, caste will be recorded ‘as declared by the respondent’. There will be a drop-down menu for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the ‘caste’ field will only cater to those in non-SC, non-ST category. The drop-down menu will only show the SC/ST list of the state where the respondent is being enumeratedThe spelling of the declared ‘caste’ will be recorded as cited by the respondent. No document or caste certificate is required to be shown to verify one’s SC, ST or ‘caste’ status. An officer said while the self-declaration template followed for the socio-economic caste census (SECC) in 2011 had thrown up over 46 lakh castes, making the data unusable, modern digital tools and AI can now surmount compilation and segregation challenges.Census Phase 2, in a first, , will collect the date and place of birth of parents, the key factors that determine citizenship/nationality.The national population register (NPR) exercise — conducted alongside Census 2011, intended to be repeated with Census 2021 before it was postponed, but now delinked from Census 2027 — had in 2010 collected details of nationality as declared by the respondent, with the rider that it would not confer any right of citizenship.Sources said the respondents will not be asked for proof of birth details of parents and these would be recorded “to the best knowledge of the respondent”. In fact, where the respondents do not know the exact date of birth of parents but only the year, a default date like January 1 of that year will be accepted.The Phase 2 questionnaire will also log passport details where available. Aadhaar number will be collected on a voluntary basis.“The purpose of collecting the birth data of parents is to know the total number of people who meet citizenship criteria based on their declaration, even though unverified. It will have no impact on the individual as the Census Act does not allow individual data to be used for “legal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,” said an officer.Self-enumeration option for Phase 2, unlike Phase 1, may allow users to submit partially-filed enumeration forms, provided a minimum number of questions are answered. “There is a realisation that even if some data fields are self-enumerated, the task of the enumerator becomes easier and less time-consuming,” said an officer.As per convention, the population enumeration exercise — which records individual data like marital status, religion, SC/ST status, occupation, migration and fertility, besides arriving at the country’s headcount — is conducted nationwide in February of the census reference year. However, it is advanced in pockets that face extreme cold and inclement weather during this window.
Article Summary: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17. caste will be recorded ‘as declared by the respondent’ and will only cater to those in non- SC, non-ST category.

Article Title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
Article Text:
SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Saying that "live-in relationships" are a reality particularly in urban areas and the law must adapt itself to serve those who choose this form of relationship and protect them from harassing partners, the Supreme Court Monday brought them under the ambit of Section 498A of the IPC or Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) where a husband or in-law shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to three years for subjecting a woman to cruelty.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. "Since the provision was aimed at solving a societal issue, it is this larger objective of securing equality for women, stepping away from the superiority of males that is an inheritance from bygone days, that has to inform the understanding in interpretation and implementation of the Section," SC said.It, however, clarified that only those "live-in relationships" which are in the nature of marriage will come within the ambit of Section 498A of IPC or Sec 85 of BNS. "Cruelty does not check at the door whether the house it's entering is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated," it said.SC, however, took note of the growing instances of alleged misuse of Section 498A. Describing as worrisome the trend of the section being misused and employed as a means of settling scores and ventilating grievances, SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those 'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection of the law."When the objective of the Section 498A was to provide coverage to those cases where harassment by husband or in-laws through wilful conduct causing mental or physical injury or driving the woman to suicide, then to say that such harassment can only be caused when they are married and not before that, in our considered view, would be a case of over simplification. Whether or not the woman in question is married or not, in the present day, does not have a proximate link to the objective of the section, which is to prevent cruelty in such a household setting," Justice Karol, who penned the verdict, said.The court said the law must respond to changing times, and bringing live-in relations within the ambit of Section 498A is needed. "Marriage was considered to be sacrosanct, which undoubtedly is a changing phenomenon. Living together, prior to marriage, is not unheard of or unacceptable anymore. In the same way, that same-sex relations, once criminalised and deemed to be a mental illness, have now been decriminalised and recognised as naturally occurring.This is the evolution of societal standards," SC said."Not a single person goes into a relationship knowing or anticipating that cruelty may be meted out to them. When a couple sets out on their journey, it is always, one presumes, with the best of intentions and to bring joyfulness of all forms. With the passage of time, however, some relationships may go down this troublesome path. The law must provide for the same. This distinction between "married" and "live-in relationship in the nature of marriage", in as much as it relates to the protection envisaged by Section 498A, has no rational nexus with the object of preventing domestic violence and is as such offensive to Article 14 of the Constitution," the bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women. Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection.

Article Title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS subscribers: Government
Article Text:
Several states governed by opposition had stopped contributing to NPS and wanted to opt out, prompting Centre to put in place UPS from April 2025

NEW DELHI: For all the noise demanding an assurance on pension, Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for central govt employees has received low traction.Data shared with Parliament Monday estimated the number of govt employees, including those who joined recently, at 1,18,195 on July 19 — which is 4.3% of the 27.6 lakh central govt number subscribers of National Pension Trust at the end of June.For long govt employees, at the Centre as well as in states, were demanding an assurance that the pension payout be at least 50% of their last salary — something that is the norm under the old pension scheme, which was discontinued in 2004 when NPS, which has contributions from the employee, kicked in.Several opposition-governed states stopped contributing to NPS and wanted to opt out, prompting the Centre to put in place UPS from April 2025. But the response to the migration option remained tepid and forced it to extend the date up to Nov 30, 2025. “…govt allowed central govt employees, who opted for UPS, one-time one-way switch facility to revert to NPS,” finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman told Parliament Monday.Along with assured 50% pension, govt also introduced retirement gratuity and death gratuity with pension benefit available to the family upon the death of the subscriber during service.Besides, those with minimum qualifying service of 10 years, are eligible to assured minimum monthly payout of Rs 10,000 on retirement.“...to date, there is no proposal under consideration to...make any changes or replace UPS,” FM said.In response to another question on July 20, govt had told Parliament that 25,756 retired central govt subscribers were eligible to receive additional benefits under UPS.
Article Summary: For long govt employees, at the Centre as well as in states, were demanding an assurance that the pension payout be at least 50% of their last salary. Several opposition-governed states stopped contributing to NPS and wanted to opt out, prompting Centre to put in place UPS from April 2025.

Article Title: South drives CM wealth surge as four leaders hold 91% of assets
Article Text:
Analysis of ADR report

South pulls the wealth map

Analysing the assets held by CMs

Same party, different worlds

Younger leaders, uneven party trend

India now has younger CMs

Degrees stay broadly stable

Cases rise, but cluster in five names

Criminal cases against CMs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of India’s chief ministers. Yet the Association for Democratic Reforms reports show a more varied picture. The country’s CMs come from different social strata, age groups, educational backgrounds and economic profiles, even within their own parties. There is no single formula for political ascent.That is what makes the comparison between ADR’s 2025 and 2026 reports more revealing than either report viewed alone. The 2025 study examined 30 chief ministers, since Manipur was then under President’s Rule. The 2026 report covers 31, after the return of a chief minister in the state. More importantly, the occupants of the chief minister’s office changed in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and West Bengal.The combined assets declared by India’s chief ministers rose from Rs 1,632 crore in the 2025 report to Rs 3,660 crore in 2026. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four.In 2025, N Chandrababu Naidu, with assets of Rs 931.84 crore, and Pema Khandu , with Rs 332.57 crore, were the only billionaire chief ministers. Siddaramaiah was a distant third with Rs 51.94 crore. A year later, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar is the clear number one with Rs 1,413.8 crore, while cine star and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay declared assets of Rs 648.86 crore. Together, these four account for approximately Rs 3,327 crore, or 90.9% of the assets declared by all 31 chief ministers. The remaining 27 account for only around Rs 333 crore between them.A geographical cut makes the imbalance sharper. Using a broad four-zone grouping, not an ADR classification, the South has only six of the 31 CMs but accounts for roughly Rs 3,059 crore, or about 83.6% of all declared CM assets in 2026. That is because three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states. So the South, in a way, lives up to the larger-than-life CM personalities. Naidu is a veteran politician who has survived many ebbs to rise again and regain his lost glory. D K Shivakumar finally got rewarded after a power tussle with Siddaramaiah, and Vijay was the new kid on the block who broke through the DMK-AIADMK binary, while also ticking the box of another cine star to become CM of Tamil Nadu. So the profiles of these billionaire CMs could not be more different.East and the Northeast together have the largest number of CMs in this grouping, 12, but account for about Rs 495 crore, helped substantially by Khandu’s declaration. North and Central India together have 10 CMs but only around Rs 75 crore in declared assets, while the West has three CMs and around Rs 31 crore.The party-wise picture is just as uneven. The BJP has 17 chief ministers in the 2026 list, but they are far from a single economic bloc. Its richest CM is Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore in declared assets. Its poorest is West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, with about Rs 85.88 lakh. That is a nearly 387-fold gap within the same party.The Congress spread is smaller in headcount but sharper in scale. Of its four CMs, Shivakumar alone accounts for Rs 1,413.8 crore. At the other end is Kerala CM V D Satheesan, with Rs 6.66 crore. Revanth Reddy , at Rs 30.05 crore, and Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh, at Rs 7.82 crore, sit far below Shivakumar’s level. In effect, Congress’s CM asset profile is overwhelmingly shaped by one leader.This is why the average can mislead. A calculation based on individual entries puts the 2026 median at only around Rs 8.23 crore, barely higher than the 2025 median of about Rs 8.02 crore.Total declared liabilities rose from roughly Rs 242 crore in 2025 to nearly Rs 505 crore in 2026, though the number of CMs declaring liabilities of Rs 1 crore or more remained unchanged at 11. Khandu led the 2025 liability table with Rs 180.28 crore. In 2026, Shivakumar moved to the top with Rs 265.07 crore, followed by Khandu and Himanta Biswa Sarma.The leadership profile also became younger. In 2025, 12 of the 30 chief ministers were in the 51-60 group. By 2026, that number had risen to 17. The number aged 61 or above fell from 10 to six. The 41-50 category remained unchanged at eight.The average reported age declined from 58.8 to 56.7, though the median remained 56. The shift reflects the exit of several older CMs, including Siddaramaiah, Pinarayi Vijayan, Nitish Kumar , M K Stalin and Mamata Banerjee. The ages are those recorded when election affidavits were filed, not necessarily current ages. So the actual decline is much sharper because the 2025 calculation accounted for many outgoing CMs’ 2021 affidavits.Here again, parties differ internally. Congress’s four CMs are tightly bunched. Revanth Reddy is 56, Sukhvinder Singh 58, Shivakumar 60 and Satheesan 61. The BJP’s spread is wider. It has Pema Khandu at 44 and Manik Saha at 70, with several CMs clustered in their 50s. In other words, the Congress CM cohort is smaller and more middle-aged, while the BJP’s larger pool stretches from younger leadership to older veterans.There was a reversal on gender. The 2025 report listed two women among 30 chief ministers. The 2026 report lists only one among 31. Mamata Banerjee’s exit from the CM roster left Delhi’s Rekha Gupta as the sole woman in the group.Many of the politicians are products of student politics. They may not have worked professionally, but they still believed in the inherent importance of formal education. In 2025, 25 of the 30 CMs were graduates, professional graduates, postgraduates or doctorate holders. In 2026, the number remained 25, despite the larger group. The proportion with graduate-level qualification or higher slipped slightly, from about 83% to 81%.Within parties, the BJP shows the widest educational spread. Its CM list includes doctorate holders such as Mohan Yadav, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Samrat Choudhary, but also leaders listed as Class 10 pass, diploma holders, graduates, professional graduates and postgraduates. Congress’s four CMs are more compact educationally: Shivakumar and Sukhvinder Singh are postgraduates, Revanth Reddy is a graduate and Satheesan is a graduate professional.The criminal-record figures worsened modestly. In 2025, 12 of 30 chief ministers, or 40%, had declared criminal cases; 10 had cases classified by ADR as serious. By 2026, 14 of 31, or 45%, had declared criminal cases; 11 had serious cases.The combined number of declared cases rose from 187 to 195. The burden remained concentrated. Revanth Reddy continued to head the list with 89 cases, followed by Suvendu Adhikari with 29, Shivakumar and Naidu with 19 each, and Kerala’s V D Satheesan with 18. Five chief ministers accounted for 174 of the 195 cases, or 89.2%.Three of Congress’s four CMs are among the top five by declared cases: Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar and Satheesan. Among BJP CMs, Adhikari carries the highest declared case load, while several BJP chief ministers have no declared criminal cases. Geography shows a similar concentration, though for different reasons. The six southern CMs together account for 147 declared cases, driven mainly by Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar, Naidu and Satheesan. East and the Northeast account for 38 cases, led by Adhikari. North and Central India account for six, while the West accounts for four. It is perhaps not a coincidence that many of the CMs with high case loads were opposition leaders for a significant time.Thus, criminal cases need to be treated with caution. A low case count may not strictly be a virtue; it may just be a case of friendly police administration.Disclosures aren’t the only way to understand the nature of a politician. But they are an important starting point, particularly when compared over the years, to understand how the seat of power remains the same, but the nature of those who occupy it changes, perhaps as an inevitable reflection of the realities of the times.
Article Summary: The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. Three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states.

Article Title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
Article Text:
Samyukt Kisan Morcha announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of student protests at Jantar Mantar, Samyukt Kisan Morcha - the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago - announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation; a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness; scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs 31,000 for workers and restoration of the old rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, Seed Bill 2025 and NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition."The protests will not be called off till all seven demands are accepted," said P Krishnaprasad of AIKS.
Article Summary: Samyukt Kisan Morcha announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26. The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation.

Article Title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
Article Text:
Deceased donor transplants still far short of demand

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation’s (NOTTO) annual report. The figure marks a fourfold rise from 4,990 transplants in 2013.Delhi-NCR recorded the highest number of transplants in 2025 with 4,564 procedures, followed by Tamil Nadu (2,796), Maharashtra (2,136), Telangana (1,523) and Kerala (1,489). Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152).India has emerged as the world’s third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China.India continues to rank first globally in living donor organ transplants, according to Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation report released in 2026.The 20,000-mark milestone coincided with the 16th Indian Organ Donation Day, when health ministry announced that more than five lakh Aadhaar-verified organ donation pledges have been recorded since the national digital pledge portal was launched in 2023.Despite the gains, deceased organ donation remains India’s biggest challenge. Deceased donor transplants rose from 837 in 2013 to 3,526 in 2025, but continue to fall far short of demand. “A substantial gap still exists between demand for organs and their availability. Addressing this gap remains a national priority,” MoS for health Anupriya Patel said.To strengthen the programme, govt launched ‘Jug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaan’, a year-long awareness campaign, besides rolling out e-Pratyaropan, a digital platform for donor registration, waitlist management and organ allocation, NOTTO mobile app, and new Brain Stem Death Certification and Swap Transplantation guidelines.Govt has also expanded transplant services, with 10 new AIIMS now performing kidney transplants, while AIIMS Bhopal has started heart transplantation and AIIMS Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Patna, Rishikesh have launched liver transplant programmes.The report highlights reforms under ‘One Nation, One Policy’ initiative, including removal of domicile requirements, the upper age limit and registration fees for patients seeking deceased donor organs. With nearly 1.73 lakh road traffic fatalities every year, the report says India has significant potential to increase deceased organ donation.
Article Summary: India has emerged as the world’s third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152)

Article Title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rejecting Meta's apology for taking down a PM Narendra Modi's video, a parliamentary committee Monday sought a personal apology from its founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg and warned of seeking removal of its safe harbour protection if he failed to comply, its chairperson Nishikant Dubey said.Dubey said removal of the PM's video was either a serious failure of the system or there "is a deliberate attempt to tarnish the image of the PM" on part of Meta."If this is how they deal with the official post of the PM, what can the common people of India expect? This failure cannot be dismissed merely as a technical error. It is a serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side. And if he does not apologise, safe harbour protection should be taken back from them," Dubey said.Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the Dubey-led committee on communications and IT, besides home secretary Govind Mohan and IT secretary S Krishnan.Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deep fake investment scams, and targeting of women, with Meta being particularly at the receiving end of their ire.While some opposition MPs emphasised that social media must retain space of dissent and 'anti-govt' content should not be considered 'anti-national', the committee was unanimous in asking for stricter and timely measures against the content that are in violation of their own stated policies, especially involving CSAM, cyber frauds, and harassment of women."We are unanimous and non-partisan on all issues," Dubey said, adding that even MHA's communications is ignored by these platforms.The BJP MP referred to the high online viewership grabbed by CJP during its recent protest, saying it, at 27 million, was more than the combined viewership of parties like BJP, Congress, AAP and SP. He blamed the platforms' choice of algorithm favouring new entrants for this.Some MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Social media platforms can amplify or suppress any content's reach, remove it or attach community notes that carry abuses, and then the question is whether they are mere intermediaries as they claim or publishers, Dubey said."It is disturbing that in 2025 alone approximately 28.15 lakh cybercrime complaints were reported nationally, with estimated losses of nearly Rs 22,495 crore," he added.
Article Summary: Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content. MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth. Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the committee on communications and IT.

Article Title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
Article Text:
In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study.

NEW DELHI: Amid growing demand to make the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) study report on E20 fuel's impact on E10-compatible vehicles public, govt agencies are looking at the possibility to release it to help remove misconceptions among vehicle users .TOI has learnt that since specific two-wheelers and cars were used for the study, details of models may not be disclosed considering commercial interest of vehicle manufacturers. "Govt has referred to the study and its findings to respond to questions in Parliament. Hence, there is a view that it should be made public so that people see that E20 fuel doesn't impact engines," said an official.In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study. The report was submitted in June 2024. The study had concluded that in case of E10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement. In the case of BS-IV cars, fuel consumption increased by 2-4%, and 2-3% in case of BS-VI-compliant cars.
Article Summary: In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study. The study had concluded that in case of E10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has suspended the licence of a packaged drinking water manufacturer in Tripura and prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of a dietary food supplement made by a Punjab-based company after inspections found serious food safety and regulatory violations.The licence of M/S Matri Drinking Water, Gomati, Tripura, was suspended with immediate effect following a complaint about foreign material in packaged drinking water. Article Title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
Article Text:
FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky. Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend.It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. It said the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers. The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself.

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security and technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability and the effective application of rules and regulations.Addressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in Delhi on Aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.Rajnath underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas — policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences.“Military officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory.When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,” Rajnath said.Explaining with the example of ‘cyber warfare’, the minister stated that if officers of the AFHQ civilian services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the defence forces. He said a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, AFHQ civilian services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.Rajnath called upon the AFHQ civilian services to evolve into the “strategic brain” of India’s defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.While he acknowledged the AFHQ civilian services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.“A military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. NEW DELHI: India’s one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the country’s 101st such site and the state’s first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.“Every new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,” said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.“From 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,” said Yadav.Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.
Article Summary: India's one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the country's 101st such site and the state’s first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.

NEW DELHI: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has revamped the "TRAI MyCall', a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. A citizen-centric digital platform that allows telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers (TSPs) information on areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures.TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system; reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action; automatic post-call feedback and coverage test feature to assess signal strength.TRAI chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: “Every telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.”“With over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling remains the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. Article Title: Pregnancy found growing near kidneys in rare medical case

NEW DELHI: Doctors in Delhi have successfully treated a woman diagnosed with an extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys, using minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery.The woman, from Bengaluru, had initially presented for a routine pregnancy evaluation. During an ultrasound, doctors detected a 10-12 cm cystic structure, which was initially suspected to be a dermoid cyst because it appeared to contain fetal parts. However, an MRI revealed a far more unusual diagnosis.The scan showed uterine dehiscence, in which the uterine wall had ruptured, allowing the pregnancy to develop in the retroperitoneal space, close to the kidneys and major blood vessels, including the aorta and inferior vena cava. Doctors found a 12-week fetus measuring about 7-8 cm inside the cyst.Dr Mannan Gupta, Founder and Chairman, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Elantis Healthcare, said the pregnancy was neither inside the uterus nor in the fallopian tube or ovary, where most ectopic pregnancies occur."Initially, the ultrasound findings suggested a dermoid cyst. However, MRI revealed an exceptionally rare condition. The pregnancy was located in the retroperitoneal space near the kidneys and major blood vessels.This is one of the rarest forms of pregnancy and the first such case I have encountered in my career," he said.Doctors performed the procedure laparoscopically, avoiding a major abdominal incision. Given the proximity of the pregnancy to vital organs and major blood vessels, the surgery required meticulous planning and precision. Doctors said the patient had an excellent postoperative outcome.According to the treating doctors, retroperitoneal pregnancy is estimated to occur in about one in 30,000 pregnancies. They said early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical, as delayed treatment can result in life-threatening complications because of the pregnancy's proximity to major blood vessels and vital organs.
Article Summary: Doctors in Delhi have successfully treated a woman diagnosed with an extremely rare pregnancy. The pregnancy developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys. Doctors performed the procedure laparoscopically, avoiding a major abdominal incision. retroperitoneal pregnancy is estimated to occur in about one in 30,000 pregnancies.

It says there are 36 separate accounts which are not seized. That is factually incorrect.”Raju opposed the submissions and informed the bench that an investigation was underway. We are preventing it,” the ASG added.When Raju claimed there was a “continuous offence”, Sibal countered the submission and questioned how such an argument could be made when the bank accounts had already been frozen.The bench was informed that the high court had appointed a former Calcutta high court judge as a special officer to oversee the operation of the three bank accounts for meeting the day-to-day expenses of running the political party.It was during this discussion that the Supreme Court suggested whether some amount could be released in favour of the special officer to meet the party’s daily expenses.The ED froze the three bank accounts, with a combined balance of Rs 440.42 crore, as part of its money laundering probe stemming from an FIR registered by the West Bengal Police over alleged dishonest financial transactions, unlawful collection of funds and routing of suspected money through certain party accounts.In its order, the high court had noted that apart from the three accounts placed under a “debit-freeze” by the ED, there were 36 other accounts in the party’s name, with around Rs 164 crore lying in them.Subsequently, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the TMC approached the high court challenging the initiation of ECIR (Enforcement Case Information Report) proceedings by the ED, which is equivalent to an FIR.According to officials, the ED’s preliminary investigation found that around Rs 160 crore was transferred from TMC’s bank accounts to Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd and its related entity between April 2023 and June 2026.The company allegedly further routed Rs 82.96 crore to another newly incorporated entity during the same period.Officials claimed that a “significant” amount was transferred to this entity, of which Rs 112 crore was allegedly used for purchasing an Embraer Legacy 600 business jet and an AgustaWestland 109SP helicopter.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, in an interview with journalist Barkha Dutt, said he received a scholarship from Boston University and also took an education loan to pursue his studies in the United States amid questions raised by RTI activist Amit Tiwari over his education expenses.Dipke's remarks came after Tiwari sought an investigation into the finances of Bhagwanrao Dipke, Abhijeet Dipke's father, questioning how a junior engineer's salary could have supported his son's higher education in the US.Addressing the controversy, Dipke said his education was funded through a combination of a scholarship and a loan.He also said that CJP plans to rely on crowdfunding and will maintain transparency while seeking financial support from people."The CJP will do crowdfunding where we will ask people for money, and we will be very transparent," Dipke said.Earlier, Tiwari had filed complaints with multiple authorities, including the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), over CJP's legal status and the tax implications of a Rs 1 crore fund pledged by Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal for the organisation.On Thursday, Tiwari said he had filed complaints at three different locations."I have filed a complaint at three different locations. I have complained against CJP at ECI. Regarding the Rs 1 Crore fund by Kapil Sibal, I have complained to CBIC (Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs) that 18% GST be levied on it," Tiwari said.He also said a complaint has been submitted to the Maharashtra government seeking an inquiry into the financial assets of Bhagwanrao Dipke, who he claimed was a Junior Engineer with the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC)."I have also complained to the Maharashtra Government that Bhagwanrao Dipke was a Junior Engineer at MIDC. Article Title: Centre raises windfall tax on petrol, diesel and ATF exports from August 3
Article Text: The Centre has once again revised the windfall tax on fuel exports, raising duties on petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for the next fortnight while keeping domestic fuel duties unchanged.According to a finance ministry notification, the revised special additional excise duty (SAED) will come into force from August 3.The SAED on diesel exports has been increased to Rs 25.5 per litre from Rs 15.5 per litre. The levy on ATF exports has been raised to Rs 22 per litre from Rs 14.5 per litre, while the duty on petrol exports has gone up to Rs 3.5 per litre from Rs 2.5 per litre, the rate notified on July 16.There is, however, no change in the duty rates on petrol and diesel cleared for domestic consumption.The export duty on diesel and ATF was first imposed on March 27 as tensions in the Middle East escalated. Since then, the government has been reviewing and revising the rates every fortnight. Petrol exports were brought under the levy from May 16.The windfall tax was introduced to ensure that adequate quantities of petroleum products remain available within the country during the Middle East crisis. It was also intended to prevent exporters from benefiting from the price gap created after global crude oil prices climbed following the outbreak of the conflict.The latest revision in export duties follows a reduction in commercial Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices that came into effect from August 1.For the second consecutive month, the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder was lowered, offering relief to restaurants, hotels, caterers and other commercial users dependent on LPG for their daily operations.The price was cut by Rs 202 per cylinder in Delhi and Rs 209 in Kolkata. After the revision, a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder is priced at Rs 2,728 in Delhi and Rs 2,872.50 in Kolkata.Last week, Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired an extended meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) with senior ministers to assess the impact of conflicts around the Strait of Hormuz, the Black Sea, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden on India's imports and supply chains.The meeting was attended by defence minister Rajnath Singh, home minister Amit Shah, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, along with special invitees chemicals and fertilisers minister JP Nadda, commerce minister Piyush Goyal, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal and petroleum minister Hardeep Puri.According to official sources, the discussions covered the security implications of the ongoing global conflicts and the disruptions they have caused to supply chains that pass through these regions.
Article Summary: The windfall tax was introduced to ensure adequate quantities of petroleum products remain available within the country during the Middle East crisis. It was also intended to prevent exporters from benefiting from the price gap created after global crude oil prices climbed following the outbreak of the conflict. There is, however, no change in the duty rates on petrol and diesel cleared for domestic consumption.

Article Title: West Bengal woman goes to check for LPG subsidy, finds Rs 100 crore in bank account
Article Text: KOLKATA: Kashmira Sheikh, 36, visited the Kultali Jamtala branch of PNB in Bengal’s South 24 Parganas to check whether the subsidy for her LPG cylinder had come through. She froze at the sound of what the bank official said was the latest “credit” to her account — Rs 99,99,99,997.She lives in an asbestos-roofed house and does zari embroidery to supplement her husband’s income from sewing bags, now has to deal with the additional shock of her lone bank account being frozen pending an inquiry ­into the mysterious deposit, Rs 3 short of Rs 100 crore.Turns out she isn’t the only one to have money they can’t use credited to their accounts, unofficially attributed to a suspected server malfunction affecting banking transactions across Bengal.Nupur Gupta, who owns a cloud kitchen in Kolkata’s Beleghata, was dragged into a joint police, bank and income tax department investigation after an unexplained deposit of Rs 47 crore in her account. She reported the transaction last Friday.PNB officials said that the “issue” was under review but the bank is yet to make any ­official statement.
Article Summary: Kashmira Sheikh, 36, visited the Kultali Jamtala branch of PNB in Bengal’s South 24 Parganas to check whether the subsidy for her LPG cylinder had come through. She froze at the sound of what the bank official said was the latest ‘credit’ to her account. Nupur Gupta, who owns a cloud kitchen in Kolkata's Beleghata, was dragged into a joint police, bank and income tax department investigation.

Article Title: Why are our cities digging the same roads again and again?
Article Text:
A familiar urban nightmare played out across India

Too many agencies, too little planning

The economic cost is far greater than building bills

Road congestion is becoming an invisible urban tax

Repeated excavation also deteriorates road quality

The problem can be mitigated by digital mapping, and common utility corridors

Growing cities need smarter governance, not more infrastructure





Every year, just after a road is opened to traffic, excavators return. The municipality may resurface a stretch only to see it dug up within weeks to lay a water pipeline, fix a sewer, lay an electricity cable, expand a gas network or pull fibre-optic lines for telecommunications companies.The cycle is so frequent that for millions of commuters, road digging is a permanent feature, not an occasional inconvenience.While authorities often point to pressing infrastructure needs, urban planners say the real problem lies in the lack of coordination among the multiple agencies responsible for India’s fast-growing cities.Whether it is Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune or Kolkata, residents are used to navigating through barricades, diversions and half-dug roads. Many times, a road paid for with public funds is good for one season, and then another department digs it up.Municipal corporations usually look after road maintenance, while water supply, sewerage boards, electricity distribution companies, gas utilities and telecom operators are often run separately, each to their own timetable with little synchronisation.The result is more digging up of the same bit of road, long traffic jams and roads that never really recover even after they have been mended.The urban experts have long argued that India’s infrastructure challenge is no longer simply one of building assets but of managing them through better coordination.The problem is even worse in large metropolitan areas where responsibility for underground infrastructure is split among dozens of government departments and utility providers. Municipal corporations build and maintain roads, water departments replace pipelines, electricity utilities lay underground cables, city gas distributors expand piped natural gas networks and telecom companies continue to install fibre networks to meet the growing demand for data.Each project may be justified in its own right, but done without a common calendar and without common digital mapping, roads are dug up time and time again. Some cities have tried to introduce “common utility corridors” or integrated utility maps, but implementation has been patchy as agencies often operate under different governments, funding mechanisms and contractors.The visible repair costs are much lower than the costs of digging up the road time and time again. India consumes over 50 billion litres of petrol every year, apart from significant diesel consumption by commercial vehicles, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Traffic engineers estimate the increased congestion created by road works causes a major rise in fuel wastage as vehicles are left idling in queues or crawling through bottlenecks.Transport researchers have shown time and again that stop-and-go traffic can increase fuel consumption by 20-40% compared to free-flowing conditions, and also lead to higher emissions. Even a small fraction of the fuel used in cities due to recurring excavation-related congestion, the economic cost of wasted fuel, lost productivity and increased vehicle maintenance amounts to thousands of crore every year.Most often the biggest loss is not money, but time. Traffic congestion is becoming one of the costliest urban problems in India, especially in cities where millions of people commute every day. Bengaluru is consistently ranked among the most traffic-congested cities in the world in global traffic studies, while Delhi, Mumbai and Pune also see significant delays during peak hours.Unplanned excavations cut road capacity, force traffic detours and create bottlenecks that last weeks, even months. Delivery times for business are affected, emergency vehicle access is impeded, and commuters are delayed on their journeys, all of which can lead to productivity and stress issues. More and more, economists talk about congestion as an “invisible tax” that cities impose on their own residents.Road engineers say a road that’s dug up and repaired won’t be as strong as it was structurally unless it is rebuilt to strict standards. Over time, trenches often settle unevenly, creating depressions, potholes and rough patches that are exacerbated during the monsoon.Badly repaired joints leak water, weakening the road base and accelerating deterioration. Then the municipalities spend public money repaving the same roads only to have them ripped open later for yet another utility project. This cyclical process increases maintenance costs and shortens the useful life of valuable taxpayer-funded road infrastructure.Many countries require agencies to coordinate projects before resurfacing a road, and have produced detailed underground utility maps for reducing repeated excavation. Some Indian cities have started experimenting with Geographic Information System (GIS)-based utility mapping and integrated permissions and common utility ducts allowing multiple services to share underground corridors.The Union government’s Smart Cities Mission also encouraged digital urban infrastructure planning in a number of cities. But experts say the problem will not be solved by technology alone unless all utility agencies are required by law to share project schedules and to complete underground work before roads are rebuilt. Absent mandatory coordination, digital platforms may become yet another government initiative underutilized.India’s urban population is expected to cross 600 million by 2036, putting unprecedented pressure on roads and underground utilities, according to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. As cities expand, water supply, electricity, gas and telecom networks are still being expanded and excavation is inevitable.The question is whether these projects can be planned in parallel instead of separately. Every unnecessary road cut is a waste of public money, a waste of fuel, a waste of emissions, and a waste of countless hours of traffic. Indian cities are spending billions on new infrastructure, but the challenge is no longer just building roads, but making sure they are dug only once, with every agency working from the same plan.
Article Summary: Roads are dug up repeatedly in India, causing traffic jams and lost productivity. Urban planners blame a lack of coordination among the multiple agencies responsible for India’s fast-growing cities. India consumes over 50 billion litres of petrol every year, apart from significant diesel consumption by commercial vehicles.

Calling the airport a key milestone in the state's growth story, the PM said the NDA government was working at "double speed"for the state's development.During his address, the Prime Minister also took a veiled swipe at the Gandhi family, saying airports in the past were often named after "a single family". Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh's Vizianagaram district. Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:
Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security

'First selection' after Modi became PM

Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security. He said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The programme is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan. India is not among them. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is published in the Federal Register.
